correctness.rationale: In ZFC, each operator has a set of argument positions; well-founded formula trees may be infinitely branching but have no infinite branch. If every arity is finite, every formula parse tree is finitely branching and well-founded, hence finite by König lemma, even with infinitely many symbols; filtration through its finite subformulas (including nullary modalities) gives a finite model and respects existential tuple witnesses. If one arity I is infinite, inject natural indices j(n) into I and designate a position a. Define a derived unary E diamond via the designated coordinate, then χ_n=E^n top ∧ ¬E^(n+1) top, pairwise inconsistent in all frames. One infinitely branching atom-free Δ_o formula puts χ_n at coordinates j(n), forcing infinitely many distinct successor worlds. The exact countable model uses natural-number chain n→n-1 and a root tuple r assigning coordinate j(n) to n, so the sharp minimum is aleph_0. Source finite checker only tests truncations arities1..9. Independently checked disjoint finite-chain height truth sets; proof for infinite syntax is deductive.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge PASS for the precise if-and-only-if under unrestricted existential-tuple semantics with well-founded infinitary arity. Classical finite filtration is prior, as are general modal infinitary operators and the infinitely-branching syntax in Girlando–Montesi. An infinity diamond explicitly quantifies over infinitely many successors, but here ordinary existential tuple binds infinitely many distinct height types without a special infinity connective. Full texts of relevant general infinitary language papers were not all accessible, leaving a real residual domination risk.
